newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli bonds close almost unchanged.
newsitem.headline: Israeli bonds close almost unchanged.

text.p: Israeli bonds closed almost unchanged on Thursday, with traders saying the market remains in a holding pattern.
* Unlinked government bonds (Gilon -- issued for four years): +0.03 pct to 173.0
* Bank of Israel short-term Makam bills: +0.03 pct to 162.98.
Volume was high at 184 million shekels with most of the activity concentrated in the Makams.
"The market was very quiet today. The market made a nice move and now it has stabilized. Investors prefer to wait for fresh news," said a trader at Bank Leumi.
"The market is likely to remain at its current level for the time being," said Elisha Rosenfeld at Lehava Investments.
CPI-linked bonds were mixed in what traders termed directionless trading.
"Unlinked bonds and Makams rose slightly but the rise was meaningless as trading was very balanced," said the Leumi trader.
Dollar-linked bonds closed lower but traders said volume was very low.
Note: Makams are zero-coupon unlinked certificates with durations of three months to one year. The Bank of Israel issues Makams to absorb liquidity.
